steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: This is the first time you've shown, since that young acolyte of yours glared at me last week.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: It's not easy, managing Endymion Temple and the rebuilding of the First Temple at the same time.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Folia is just worried that I'm overworked. She knows we've been friends since our priest school days.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Which made it all the harder to accept that I brought you trouble as soon as I got back, I guess.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Pallas...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I knew we were both in trouble when you showed up at Endymion Temple to have your dream interpreted as an ordinary Minoan instead of using the priests' passage, six months ago.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: In most cases, divine revelation can be classified into certain common categories, whether it came in the form of a dream or a sudden vision.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I know. We learned them by heart at school, so ordinary priests without special talents could guide those who received revelations.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: But the vision that you brought was not found in any classic tale... I had no doubt that it was a powerful revelation, which made me very uneasy.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Don't worry. We'll find a way.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You shouldn't have quit the priesthood. You might have been able to find help...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And hide my condition, continuing to be the legendary 'Goddess of Victory' on the border?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I didn't want to complicate things, even if another has taken up the title. Besides, the heroes came a long way to call me back. I had to be honest with myself.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: ...Looks like Rhodes Island has treated you well.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Of course. Did I ever tell you that I founded a 'Minoan League' on Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Are there so many Minoans who left home to seek treatment?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: There are plenty, although Erato and Vulcan are the only true Minoans in the league. The others are in it because they have a spiritual fascination with our country.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I'll introduce them, when we have a chance. They're all full of heroic spirit, with great passion for poetry, art, and brewing.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: So you founded a drinking league.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: That's one way to put it. It's not quite the same as having you around, though. You may not hold your drink particularly well, but no one in our year brewed better than you.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I remember how you tied up your sleeves and pounded the grapes like a seasoned winemaker at the intercollegiate conference. You looked amazing.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I see you have a craving. What happened to the formula I gave you?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I lost it when I went to Akroti. I finally escaped my torment when my Sarkaz bodyguard gave me the recipe for the secret brew of Kazdel.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I never worried you would have trouble making friends. First the Sarkaz bodyguard, now the Sargonian ambassador.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You heard about the fruit farmers and the craftsmen. Titi can be trusted.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I don't doubt Kyría Mashayer's cleverness, or her friendly outlook towards our country, but her position remains sensitive.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: If I didn't stop you, would you have put her in charge of the play that we already discussed, in addition to the venue of the exchange ceremony?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Is it that you trust her too much, or...?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You're frowning again, Kassandra. I just let myself get a little lazy, having been away from the priesthood for so long.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You would never have become a legend in the borderlands, if you were the type to shirk responsibility.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I don't mind taking charge of the rebuilding project on your behalf. I just think it's a shame. You're better at dealing with people, and the craftsmen trust you.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I thought you made the proposal to the people so they would return to heroic tradition and remember the heroic spirit.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And that's exactly why it doesn't matter who's in charge.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Our people venerate the heroes, but they've gradually forgotten that Minoan prosperity was not only built by a few heroes.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: 'The heroes came from the people, from all walks of life.'

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You could always read my mind.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I know what you're trying to say... but with the rebuilding of the temple entering its final stage, it's even more important than ever to have a supervisor.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I think we'll have one soon.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I saw Lydia headed to the temple square.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What do you think this Astynomos, who has quietly been at odds with us from the beginning and is trying to take the play out of the priests' hands, is going there for?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: We meet at last, Your Excellency Ambassador Mashayer.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: And who might you be?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I'm the Astynomos of Athenius, called Lydia. I am overseeing this relic exchange between our two nations.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Oh! I'm so sorry, Astynomos. I should have visited you first thing when I got to Athenius. I didn't think...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You came into Athenius by the ancient route to follow in Kereseira's footsteps, didn't you?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: There is no need to apologize to a Minoan for your love of our epics, our culture.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: If anything, I should be thanking you for resolving the dispute between the fruit farmers and craftsmen. The rebuilding of the First Temple could not have proceeded so smoothly without you.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I simply did my part.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I believe you've already met Behnui? I take it the venue and details of the exchange ceremony have not been confirmed.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Rather than do it behind closed doors in a private room, what do you think of holding the ceremony beneath the statue of Kereseira, to be witnessed by her and all of Athenius?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You want to hold the exchange ceremony at the First Temple square?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes. You are aware that I brought the most precious treasure of the Varjavandabad Museum, to be exchanged for the technical data that the Sargonians left behind during the construction of the Three Poleis.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It's a part of many heroic Minoan stories, and closely linked to Kereseira herself.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Seeing the completed statue on the square was an awe-inspiring experience. Her brave visage and the relic that I carry complement each other.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I understand that the exchange ceremony is supposed to begin with a classical play, in accordance with Minoan tradition. What better place to do it than the First Temple's new amphitheater?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Would that be a problem?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Oh, Kassandra from Endymion Temple reminded me that any use of the First Temple should be discussed with her...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Kassandra...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: It's the Astynomos' Office's responsibility to lighten the burden on the busy priests by handling trivial matters. I'll communicate with her.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I was concerned about the lack of proper supervision in the rebuilding process because of the emulation of ancient methods, which has resulted in significant delays. I thought it might not be the most dignified of venues.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I don't mind—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: However, all our problems could be solved if you are officially made the supervisor of the rebuilding project.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Say what now?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: The rebuilding of the temple is entering its final stages. We've reached the point where decisiveness and efficiency are more important than careful planning.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I'm sure you already have a fair idea of what is going on, having befriended the craftsmen and solved their issues.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Besides, I understand that you received an advanced education in museology in Columbia, including studies in architecture.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Putting the finishing touches on the temple and readying it for opening shouldn't present too much difficulty, should it?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I mean, it's true that I designed and supervised the expansion of my museum, but it's not nearly as big as this temple...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Besides, is it really appropriate for a Sargonian ambassador to supervise the rebuilding of the First Temple?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Your request that the exchange ceremony take place at the First Temple is ample proof of your understanding of the relic and Minoan culture.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I am in full support of your proposal, and I'm sure the ever-considerate Kassandra won't object.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But...
I didn't expect the ambassador to be such a polite and humble young lady.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Períandros?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Greetings from Corinia, land of trade and merchants, Your Excellency Ambassador Mashayer of Sargon.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I am here as Corinia's representative to the exchange ceremony, at the Astynomos' request. I happened to overhear your conversation and couldn't help but stop to listen.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: May I ask you a question—would you participate in the rebuilding of the First Temple, if your status were not a concern?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It would be a great honor to participate in the restoration of such a wonderful example of Minoan architecture, not to mention the knowledge that could be gained! I would be delighted just to hew one piece of marble for it!

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: In that case, why trouble yourself unnecessarily?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Trouble myself... what?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I have a little suggestion that might solve our present problem. As I see it, the two of you are in full agreement, but for this little issue of Ambassador Mashayer's status.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: It's a sensitive issue, and Ambassador Mashayer's concerns are certainly well-founded. On the other hand, the Astynomos here is seeking a capable supervisor who has the support of the people, in order to keep the temple project on track.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: What better way to resolve this than Minos's most ancient process?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: A vote.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: A referendum held on the First Temple square. Let the citizens of Athenius participating in the rebuilding decide whether to accept Ambassador Mashayer's supervision or not.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...She's really the Sargonian ambassador.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Travesty! The theater of Kereseira's First Temple was not built to host a diplomatic farce!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: That Sargonian said she brought a relic in exchange for the technical data from the Three Poleis? I knew that cargo didn't feel like movie figurines.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The shape, the weight, and its relevance to Kereseira... could it be...?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The gall! To use stolen Minoan treasure to buy Minoan trust!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Not if I have anything to say about it...
